description:
The Bling Era , also known as the Bling Bling Era , was a club-oriented, highly commercialized period in hip-hop history, gaining popularity from the late-1990s to the mid-2000s. It was defined by maximalist fashion, unapologetic wealth and a massive shift from the underground, gritty street rap of the early 1990s to a hyper-luxurious, mainstream pop crossover sound.

By the late 1990s, the stark, grim realism of early-to-mid '90s gangsta rap had run its course. The genre was deeply traumatized by the 1996 and 1997 murders of Tupac Shakur and The Notorious B.I.G., which cast a dark cloud over the aggressive, coast-versus-coast street warfare narrative. At the same time, the brief, hyper-pop Jiggy Era (1997–1999)—championed by Bad Boy Records' shiny silver suits and Hollywood-style pop-radio crossovers—had ushered in as a precursor to the Bling Era which came in full effect by 1999-2006. The answers came from the American South, specifically New Orleans, where Cash Money Records was waiting to redefine the genre's landscape. [ 1 ]
